_: Golden behaviour of the Python `team` command, captured 13 October 2026 BEFORE porting it.
This is the trap-1 mitigation from docs/labs/d30-no-python-2026-10-13: parity.py compares Rust
against Python, so it dies when Python does. Once `team` is Rust there is no second opinion to
disagree with, so the behaviour that mattered is frozen here as literal expectations and asserted
Captured by running the Python harness against a throwaway git repo with an empty claims store and
an isolated live tier. Timestamps and short SHAs are time-dependent and are asserted by SHAPE, not
by value; every other field is asserted exactly.

claim_fields._head: a short SHA, or empty string when git cannot answer
claim_fields._claimed_at: ISO 8601 with the local UTC offset, e.g. 2026-10-13T13:35:28-04:00

refusal_other_lab_holds._stdout: team claim: probe/one is already held by lab 'claude' since 2026-10-13T13:35:28-04:00
refusal_other_lab_holds._stderr_second_line: use a different branch, or release it with: team release --branch <name>

refusal_no_lab._stderr: team claim: a lab is required (--lab), because a claim without an owner is not a claim

refusal_no_branch._stderr: team claim: a branch name is required

rules_that_are_not_obvious.same_lab_may_reclaim: claiming a branch your own lab already holds SUCCEEDS (existing['lab'] == lab is not a refusal); it refreshes the entry
rules_that_are_not_obvious.release_allows_other_lab_when_unowned: release with no --lab releases regardless of owner; release --lab X refuses when the entry's lab is not X
rules_that_are_not_obvious.release_syncs_the_removal: the live mirror is republished on release - a mirror only ever added to resurrects released claims
rules_that_are_not_obvious.claim_records_a_ledger_line: kind=claim on success only; a refused claim writes nothing
rules_that_are_not_obvious.release_records_a_ledger_line: kind=release, lab defaulting to the entry's previous owner
rules_that_are_not_obvious.empty_branch_and_lab_are_usage_errors: ValueError from claim_branch, surfaced as EXIT_USAGE, not EXIT_FAIL
